title: Cornell students and faculty protest university's handling of sexual violence allegations
seoTitle: Ithaca protest over sexual violence handling

tea.why: Students and faculty protested Cornell University's handling of alleged gang rape by fraternity members and its response to sexual violence allegations.

tea.changed: Oct 6: Hundreds of students and faculty protested at Cornell University, calling for the president's resignation and an overhaul of policies.

summary: On Monday, October 6, 2026, students and faculty members gathered at Cornell University in Ithaca, New York, to protest the university's handling of sexual violence allegations. The demonstration specifically addressed the university's and police's response to an alleged gang rape by fraternity members in 2024. Protesters called for the resignation of Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff and demanded an overhaul of how sexual assault cases are managed. Other demands included an external inquiry into the administration's actions, independent hearings, uniform minimum sanctions for sexual assaults, and improved training for campus police. President Kotlikoff stated the university was "not hiding anything" and would propose improvements. The faculty senate also announced plans for a no-confidence vote in the administration.

updates.text: Students and faculty protested at Cornell University over the handling of sexual violence allegations and an alleged gang rape by fraternity members.
Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff stated he was "not hiding anything" regarding the case and that proposals would be made to improve the culture.
The Cornell faculty senate announced plans to vote on a resolution of no confidence in the university's administration.
